title: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh, grilled with sauce, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh prepared on the grill with a flavorful sauce. The skin is removed and not consumed. The meat is tender, juicy, high in protein and contains a modest amount of fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken legs and thighs are popular in barbecue dishes because of their rich flavor.
Grilling imparts a smoky aroma and caramelizes the sauce on the surface.
Removing the skin reduces saturated fat, making the dish more diet‑friendly.
Chicken meat is a good source of vitamin B6, which is involved in protein metabolism.
Traditional grill sauces often contain honey, soy sauce, garlic and spices.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Protein is essential for tissue growth, repair and supports the immune system.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Skin‑less preparation lowers saturated fat content, benefiting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 aids amino‑acid metabolism and supports nervous system function.

items.title: Source of selenium
items.content: Selenium has antioxidant properties and supports thyroid function.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: High protein content helps maintain a feeling of fullness for longer.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Improper cooking or storage can allow bacteria such as Salmonella to grow.

items.title: Sodium in the sauce
items.content: Prepared sauces often contain high salt levels; people with hypertension should watch portions.

items.title: High grilling temperatures
items.content: Excessive charring can create harmful compounds like acrylamide and heterocyclic amines.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a main dish, slice for salads, sandwiches, or add to rice and vegetable sides. Drizzle extra sauce or garnish with fresh herbs if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked product in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before consumption.
